name: mCCP stretch reminder: message quality (v2)
task: Given one subscriber's profile, the system writes (or deliberately withholds) one WhatsApp message reminding a pregnant mother to do a stretch from Noora's clinician-reviewed knowledge bank.
output_contract: The system returns {type: 'stretch' | 'consult_first' | 'none', message: string | null}. S1 and S2 grade the type; everything else grades the message.

scoring.gates: Every check marked gate:true must pass. One gate failure fails the whole message, whatever else it does well.
scoring.pass: All gates pass AND at least 85% of the applicable non-gate checks pass.
scoring.na: A check can be N/A only where its 'applies_when' says so. N/A checks are left out of the 85%.

criteria.check: A stretch message goes only to a mother who is still pregnant on the send date: profile stage is 'pregnant' AND her expected due date (EDD) is after the send date. Every other profile gets no stretch message.
criteria.why: 405 delivered families still got pregnancy messages; EDD is the profile's key field and RCH dates can be wrong.

criteria.check: If the profile carries a medical hold flag (bed rest, high-risk, placenta previa, recent bleeding, doctor said no exercise), no stretch is suggested; the message (if any) only says to ask her doctor or a Noora nurse first.
criteria.why: Exercise is contraindicated for some pregnancies; the profile is the only place the system can know this.

criteria.check: Every stretch the message names is on the knowledge bank's approved list for the mother's trimester.
criteria.why: Only clinician-reviewed stretches reach families.

criteria.check: The instructions add no contraindicated element to the stretch: no lying flat on the back after the first trimester, no holding the breath, no bouncing, no deep twist at the belly, no stretching to the point of pain.
criteria.why: An approved stretch can still be described unsafely.

criteria.check: Tells her to stop if she has at least one named warning sign (bleeding, fluid leaking, pain, dizziness, contractions, shortness of breath, chest pain). How to reach help is S6.
criteria.why: The one thing she must never miss.

criteria.check: For warning signs, sends her to in-person care right away: names the nearest health centre or hospital, or her country's emergency number. 'Reply on WhatsApp' alone does not pass.
criteria.why: Replies to WhatsApp questions take ~69 hours on average in India; a warning sign cannot wait for that.

criteria.check: Promises no outcome: never says stretching will make delivery easy, prevent pain, prevent complications, or keep the baby healthy.
criteria.why: Outcome promises are medical claims nobody has signed off.

criteria.check: Every other health statement in the message (what the stretch helps, how often, who it is for) matches the knowledge-bank entry it came from. Ignores stage or week claims (G2) and outcome promises (S7).
criteria.why: Grounding, separate from the outcome promises in S7.

criteria.applies_when: the message mentions her week or trimester
criteria.check: Any week or month the message states matches her week computed from her EDD and the send date.
criteria.why: A wrong week tells the family the service does not know them.

criteria.check: The hold time, repetitions and total time it asks for are within the knowledge-bank range for that stretch.
criteria.why: Too much is a safety risk; too little does nothing.

criteria.check: Names one specific stretch, not 'some stretches' or 'light exercise'.
criteria.why: A vague nudge cannot be acted on.

criteria.check: Describes the starting position and the movement clearly enough to do it without a picture or video.
criteria.why: Many families read on low-bandwidth phones.

criteria.check: States how long to hold or how many times to repeat, as a number.
criteria.why: Observable, and it is the part people forget.

criteria.check: Offers a safer or easier way to do it (hold a wall or chair, sit instead of stand, do fewer if tired).
criteria.why: Bodies change week to week.

criteria.check: Ties the stretch to a moment in her day (after morning tea, after cooking, before sleep).
criteria.why: Habits stick to existing routines.

criteria.check: Ends with one yes/no practice question she can answer with a single reply (e.g. 'Were you able to try it today? Reply 1 for Yes, 2 for No').
criteria.why: Observability nudges: self-reports show whether the behaviour is being practised. ~10k of 65-70k daily recipients reply.

criteria.check: Still makes sense and is respectful if the husband or another relative reads it first (says who it is for, or asks them to share it with her).
criteria.why: 41,520 families' phones belong to a husband or relative.

criteria.check: Gives a family member one concrete way to help (stay nearby, hold her steady, remind her).
criteria.why: Noora trains family caregivers, not only the mother.

criteria.applies_when: the profile holds a fact beyond stage and name
criteria.check: Uses at least one fact from her profile beyond her stage and name (something she told Noora, her routine, her last reply).
criteria.why: 'We know a lot about our users and use almost none of it.'

criteria.check: Needs no equipment, cost or space a low-income home may not have (no gym ball, no yoga mat, no class).
criteria.why: Advice she cannot follow is noise.

criteria.check: Asks her for no new personal information (due date, phone numbers, address, health history). The yes/no practice reply in A6 is allowed.
criteria.why: Every extra data point asked for means more friction and more drop-off.

criteria.check: Written in the profile's preferred language (checked by script: Devanagari for Hindi/Marathi/Nepali, Bengali script for Bengali, Kannada script for Kannada, Latin for Bahasa Indonesia/English).
criteria.why: Noora serves families in 11 languages.

criteria.check: Fits one WhatsApp screen: 120 words or fewer.
criteria.why: Long messages go unread.

criteria.check: Average sentence length is 15 words or fewer.
criteria.why: Short sentences read and translate better.

criteria.check: Uses no term from the jargon list (supine, pelvic floor, Braxton Hicks, contraindicated, ligament, etc.) without a plain-words explanation in the same sentence.
criteria.why: Plain words for every literacy level.

criteria.check: Contains no link except an approved Noora domain, and no phone number except the approved help line.
criteria.why: Stops invented links and numbers.

criteria.check: Works when read aloud as a voice note: no abbreviations, symbols, emoji or numbered lists that carry meaning. (Links are L5.)
criteria.why: Audio is common and many families listen rather than read.

criteria.check: Contains no blame, guilt or fear (no 'if you don't stretch, your baby…', no scolding for missed days).
criteria.why: Shame makes families disengage.

criteria.check: Opens by speaking to her directly (her name, or a respectful greeting used in her language) rather than starting with an instruction.
criteria.why: Observable stand-in for 'warm'.

criteria.check: Fits the setting: examples, clothing and places match her home life (floor, chair, courtyard), with nothing that assumes a city gym or Western lifestyle.
criteria.why: Cultural fit is what makes advice feel meant for her.
